title: Bounded flat constructible total tensor on the etale site
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]). Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$ be integers. Let $P,Q$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes of these sheaves, with flat constructible terms, with $P^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ and $Q^j=0$ for $j\notin[c,d]$. Flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] means that tensoring with the term is exact; constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] means locally constant with finite $A$-module values on each stratum of a finite constructible locally closed stratification. Form the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{A_X}Q)$, with $T^n=\bigoplus_{i+j=n}P^i\otimes_{A_X}Q^j$ and differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_Q$ on bidegree $(i,j)$. Then $T$ has flat constructible terms, is zero outside $[a+c,b+d]$, and every cohomology sheaf of $T$ is constructible. It is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] (tensoring an acyclic complex with it gives an acyclic total tensor), and its image in the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is isomorphic to the relative derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] of the images of $P$ and $Q$. For every $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero, $T\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}N$ has cohomology only in $[a+c,b+d]$. The zero ring, zero terms, degenerate intervals and empty scheme are allowed.

proof.text: Use the small-site universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention] for the small etale site and its module sheaves. The hypotheses give $P^i=0$ for $i>b$ and $Q^j=0$ for $j>d$, and every term is flat in the exact-tensor sense. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat], on the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{et}},A_X)$, separately to $P$ and $Q$. Both complexes are K-flat. Neither the finiteness of $A$ nor a lower bound on the complexes is needed for this step.

The complexes $P,Q$ now satisfy both hypotheses of [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]: they are K-flat and have flat terms, over the same commutative ring sheaf $A_X$. Consequently their actual signed direct-sum total tensor $T$ has flat terms and is K-flat. This is the ringed-site result, so it applies directly on the small etale site, without interpreting $A_X$ as a scheme structure sheaf or changing coefficient categories.

source.place: Tag 07A2, lemma-tensor-product-K-flat; flat terms: sites-modules.tex, Tag 0G6Q, lemma-tensor-flats

proof.text: In the total-term formula of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], a nonzero summand in degree $n$ must have $a\le i\le b$, $c\le j\le d$, and $i+j=n$. There are finitely many such pairs. If $n<a+c$ or $n>b+d$ there are none. Tensor with zero is zero, since the tensor functor preserves the initial object by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] (for a zero left factor, [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives the sheafification of the sectionwise zero tensor presheaf, hence zero). A direct sum with all but finitely many zero summands is canonically the sum of the remaining summands, by its coproduct universal property. Thus $T^n=0$ outside $[a+c,b+d]$, and each $T^n$ is a finite direct sum of the indicated tensor sheaves. These are statements about terms, not merely cohomological bounds.

source.place: Proof (1),(2), finite A: bounded total tensor of the two models; elementary degree calculation

proof.text: Fix a pair $(i,j)$ in the two input intervals and put $F=P^i$, $G=Q^j$. Choose the finite constructible locally closed stratifications in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] for $F$ and $G$. The fibre-product intersection stratification of [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] refines both and still has constructible strata. By [lemma-constructible-of-refines], both restricted sheaves are finite locally constant on every new stratum. For its immersion $u:Z\to X$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $u^{-1}A_X$ with $A_Z$ and identifies inverse image with module pullback. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] gives $u^{-1}(F\otimes_{A_X}G)\cong u^{-1}F\otimes_{A_Z}u^{-1}G$. The right side is locally constant by [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-locally-constant-part] and finite by [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-finite-part]. Here finite generation agrees with finite values because $A$ is a finite ring. Hence the displayed intersection stratification witnesses constructibility of $P^i\otimes_{A_X}Q^j$. This argument uses the actual fibre products, not factorization of an immersion inferred from set-theoretic containment.

source.place: Tag 095I, lemma-tensor-product-constructible, its common-refinement proof; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text: By [thm-constructible-serre], constructible $A_X$-modules are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions, in precisely the global finite-stratification convention used here. Zero is constructible (restrict the zero module on the one-stratum stratification; use the empty stratification if $X$ is empty). Finite sums are constructible by induction using the split short exact sequence $0\to F\to F\oplus G\to G\to0$ and the extension clause. Steps 3 and 4 therefore show that every $T^n$ is constructible. For every $n$, the kernel clause gives constructible $Z^n=\ker(d_T^n:T^n\to T^{n+1})$. Since $d_T^n d_T^{n-1}=0$, the previous differential factors through $Z^n$, and the cokernel clause applied to $T^{n-1}\to Z^n$ gives constructible $\operatorname{coker}(T^{n-1}\to Z^n)=\mathcal H^n(T)$. The equality is the kernel/image definition of cohomology in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. In particular no claim that arbitrary subsheaves of constructible sheaves are constructible is used.

source.place: Tag 03RZ, lemma-constructible-abelian, clause (3); finite sums and cohomology are the displayed elementary deductions

proof.text: Let $q$ denote localization to the ordinary unbounded derived category of $A_X$-modules. By step 1, $P,Q$ lie in the flat-term K-flat subcategory of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Its specified comparison gives $q(T)\cong q(P)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}q(Q)$. This is the relative tensor of [def-kun-derived-tensor]: take the identity K-flat resolution $P\to P$ in that definition. The independence statement of [lem-kun-derived-tensor-well-defined] identifies this computation with any other K-flat resolution used for that same tensor. All objects and comparisons are in the ordinary etale module-sheaf derived category, with the signed total differential already specified in the item.

source.place: Tags 06YT, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side, and 06YU, definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction

proof.text: For an arbitrary $A_X$-module sheaf $N$, step 2 permits [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] with $P$ there equal to $T$ here. Thus $q(T)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_X}N[0]$ is represented by the complex with degree-$n$ term $T^n\otimes_{A_X}N$ and differential $d_T^n\otimes1_N$. By step 3 these terms vanish outside $[a+c,b+d]$; tensor with zero vanishes by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. At a degree outside the interval the cycles are a subobject of the zero term and hence zero, so the kernel/image formula in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives zero cohomology there. This proves the asserted Tor interval for every $N$, without requiring $N$ to be flat or constructible.
